title: Cisco Umbrella: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Picture a hotel concierge who checks every address you ask for. If it's a known bad one, they don't let you go. That's what Umbrella does with D N S.

scenes.heading: The DNS concierge
scenes.narration: Umbrella sits in the cloud, and checks names before you connect. It's a cloud service, backed by Cisco Talos threat research. It judges each name by its reputation. Then it allows, blocks, or warns. You can point a whole network at it, or use a roaming client.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. It's a cloud service. Pointing D N S at it protects the whole network. It mainly uses domain reputation.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Umbrella filters D N S in the cloud. It judges domain reputation. Use network D N S settings or a roaming client. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva Umbrella lab.
